LESSON: SIGN READING 10.4.1 INTENSIVE SIGN READING: CHARACTERS AND THEIR TRAITS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.4: Sign Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Characters and their traits
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Characters and their traits, part of Strand 10 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How are signed oral narratives relevant in modern society?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Characters and their traits together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: Learners develop interpretation and inference skills as they discuss the lessons learned and the

relevance of monster narratives in real life.

● Citizenship: Learners develop the skill of information and communication as they reason logically in choosing the reading strategies

that would best aid in sharing experiences with community members.

● Citizenship: Learners develop the skill of ethical digital citizenship as they search online and offline for features of monster narratives

Values:
● Responsibility: is developed as learners observe safety precautions when searching online and offline for features of monster narratives.

Link to other Subjects

The learner relates the concept of characters and their traits to their learning of literary texts in Kiswahili.
